observations.text: SP flew the ASR approach at the level desired for this stage, with the IP directing the controller-issued headings and the descent point. Altitude until on final diverged by 350 feet and heading by 12 degrees before the IP prescribed the corrections. Marginal performance for the Training Section - independent tracking of the assigned headings and advisory altitudes is expected to improve.

SP flew the ASR approach to MDA without the IP executing any part of the procedure, requiring only verbal prompts at the descent point. Altitude until on final reached the 300 foot limit and heading reached 10 degrees off the assigned final approach course, recognized and corrected with delay. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP tracked the controller-issued headings and the advisory altitudes on the ASR approach without IP intervention. Altitude until on final varied by 220 feet, heading by 7 degrees and airspeed by plus 15 knots, each recognized and self-corrected in a timely manner. Level-off at MDA was 150 feet high. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the ASR approach with an accurate and rapid instrument cross-check from the initial vector to the missed approach point. Altitude until on final was held within 120 feet, heading within 4 degrees and airspeed within plus 8 / minus 3 knots, with level-off 70 feet above MDA. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the ASR approach with exceptional precision, anticipating each controller-issued heading and the descent point without prompting. Deviations in altitude until on final, heading and airspeed were negligible, and MDA was held with no measurable overshoot. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a non-standardized power and pitch technique at the descent point, did not establish the briefed rate of descent on the ASR final, with the result that altitude diverged by 380 feet until on final. Airspeed decayed 25 knots below the briefed final approach speed and the IP directed the corrections and flew part of the descent to MDA.

SP, due to inadequate workload management during the approach phase, did not complete the landing configuration before commencing descent from the final approach fix, leaving the controller-issued headings untracked. Heading diverged 18 degrees from the assigned final approach course and altitude by 400 feet until on final. The approach was completed only with the IP directing the descent and executing part of the level-off at MDA.

SP completed the ASR approach at the desired level, applying the altitude and heading corrections after the IP's verbal prompts. Altitude until on final reached the 300 foot limit twice and heading reached 10 degrees off the assigned course, with recognition delayed on each occasion. Marginal performance for the Training Section - earlier recognition of the controller-issued heading changes is expected to improve.

SP tracked the assigned headings and the advisory altitudes on the ASR approach without IP intervention. Altitude until on final varied by 230 feet and airspeed by plus 14 knots, both recognized and corrected in a timely manner, with level-off at MDA 140 feet high. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the ASR approach accurately and rapidly, complying with each controller-issued heading and descent instruction. Altitude until on final was contained within 130 feet, heading within 4 degrees and airspeed within plus 9 / minus 4 knots, with level-off 80 feet above MDA. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the ASR approach with exceptional precision and an uninterrupted instrument cross-check. Heading, altitude and airspeed deviations on the surveillance final were negligible, and MDA was captured without overshoot. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to power not reset after gear and flap extension, did not maintain the briefed final approach airspeed on the ASR approach, with the result that airspeed fell 22 knots below the briefed value and altitude diverged 400 feet until on final. The IP directed the power correction and flew part of the descent to MDA.

SP, due to an interrupted instrument cross-check while attention remained on the approach controller's transmissions, did not monitor the altimeter during the descent to MDA. The aircraft descended 120 feet below MDA before recognition. The IP intervened to arrest the descent and directed the missed approach.

SP, due to late lead points on the controller-issued turns, did not roll out on the assigned final approach course, with the result that heading was 10 degrees off course and altitude until on final reached the 300 foot limit. The corrections were applied only after the IP's verbal prompts and recognition was delayed.

SP, due to an incomplete mental model of the approach sequence that was not updated when the controller amended the final approach course, did not anticipate the descent point on the ASR approach. Altitude until on final reached the 300 foot limit and level-off at MDA was 200 feet high. Both deviations were recognized and corrected only after the IP's verbal prompts.

SP flew the ASR approach within the desired standards, tracking the controller-issued headings and the advisory altitudes without IP intervention. Altitude until on final twice reached 230 feet and airspeed twice reached plus 16 knots before self-correction, and level-off at MDA was 160 feet high. Marginal performance for the Training Section - tighter altitude control on the surveillance final is expected to improve.

SP executed the ASR approach with an accurate and rapid instrument cross-check, complying promptly with each controller-issued heading. Altitude until on final was held within 110 feet, heading within 3 degrees and airspeed within plus 8 / minus 4 knots, with level-off 60 feet above MDA. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the ASR approach with exceptional precision, anticipating the controller's turn and descent instructions. Deviations in altitude, heading and airspeed on the surveillance final were negligible and MDA was held with no measurable overshoot. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a scan sequence that left the attitude indicator as a secondary reference, did not maintain aircraft control on the ASR final, with the result that altitude diverged 420 feet until on final and heading 20 degrees from the assigned course. The IP took the aircraft and flew the approach from the descent point to MDA.

SP, due to continuation of the approach after the aircraft state had already diverged from the briefed profile, did not initiate the missed approach at the missed approach point. Airspeed was 24 knots below the briefed final approach speed and the aircraft was 130 feet below MDA before recognition. The IP directed the go-around and executed part of the missed approach procedure.

SP, due to over-controlling in pitch during the descent, did not establish a steady rate of descent on the ASR approach, with the result that altitude until on final reached the 300 foot limit and level-off at MDA was 200 feet high. The corrections were applied only after the IP's verbal prompts and recognition was delayed.

SP, due to task sequencing that concentrated the landing checklist inside the turn to final, did not track the controller-issued headings on the ASR approach. Heading reached 10 degrees off the assigned final approach course and airspeed reached plus 20 knots above the briefed value. Both were corrected only on the IP's verbal prompts, with delayed recognition.

SP, due to slow correction rates after each controller-issued heading change, did not hold the assigned final approach course precisely, with the result of deviations of 8 degrees in heading and 220 feet in altitude until on final. All deviations were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention.

SP, due to divided attention between the approach controller's transmissions and the instrument cross-check, did not maintain the briefed final approach airspeed throughout the descent. Airspeed reached plus 15 knots and level-off at MDA was 170 feet high. Both deviations were recognized and self-corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention.

SP executed the ASR approach within the desired standards, complying accurately with the controller-issued headings and the advisory altitudes. Altitude until on final was held within 140 feet and level-off at MDA was 95 feet high, values lying at the edge of the desired band. Marginal performance for the Training Section - a tighter instrument cross-check on the surveillance final is expected to improve these margins.

SP flew the ASR approach with exceptional precision, anticipating each controller-issued heading and the descent point without prompting. Deviations in altitude, heading and airspeed on the surveillance final were negligible and MDA was captured with no measurable overshoot. Above end of block MIF achieved.
